welcome_2.subject: How co-ownership actually works — and why it's not a timeshare
welcome_2.preview: How co-ownership actually works — and why it's not a timeshare.
welcome_2.main_heading: Co-Ownership Is Real Ownership — Here's How It Works
welcome_2.item01_body: When you buy through a co-ownership scheme, you receive a deeded, legally recognised fractional share of the property — typically between 1/8 and 1/2. This ownership is registered and protected in the same way as any other property purchase.
welcome_2.item02_body: Each share comes with an allocated number of weeks per year, proportional to the size of your stake. Usage is typically managed through a rota system, ensuring fair and flexible access across all owners throughout the year.
welcome_2.item03_body: Maintenance, management fees, and running costs are split equally between all owners. This means you benefit from a premium, fully managed property at a fraction of what it would cost to own — and maintain — outright.
welcome_2.item04_title: You Can Sell Whenever You Choose
welcome_2.item04_body: There are no lock-in periods and no membership to cancel. If you decide to sell your share — whether in a year or a decade — you can do so on the open market, just like any other property. Any capital growth is yours to keep.
welcome_2.faq_label: The most common question we get:
welcome_2.faq_body_1: It's genuinely different — and the distinction matters. A timeshare gives you the right to use a property for a fixed period each year; you don't own anything, you can rarely sell your stake freely, and the whole arrangement is tied to a membership or points system that can be altered by the operator.
welcome_2.faq_body_2: Co-ownership is deeded property ownership. You hold a registered legal title to a share of the property itself. You can sell your share on the open market to any buyer you choose, at any time. There are no points, no memberships, and no annual fees beyond the actual cost of running the home.

nurture_day14.subject: Your co-ownership questions, answered
nurture_day14.preview: Still thinking it over? Here's what other buyers wanted to know first.
nurture_day14.main_heading: A Few Things Worth Knowing Before You Decide
nurture_day14.intro_body: I know buying a share in a property is a significant decision, and it's not one to rush. I wanted to share a few things that often help people feel more confident before they take the next step.
nurture_day14.faq1_body: You own a legal deeded share of the property, registered in your name. This is a genuine real-estate asset — not a timeshare or points-based scheme.
nurture_day14.faq2_title: What if I want to sell my share?
nurture_day14.faq2_body: You can sell at any time on the open market, just like any other property. There are no lock-in periods and no restrictions on resale.
nurture_day14.faq3_body: Running costs — maintenance, insurance, management — are shared equally between owners and are fully disclosed upfront. There are no surprises.
nurture_day14.closing_body: If you'd like to talk it through, just reply to this email. No obligation — genuinely.
nurture_day14.signoff_body: If any of these resonate, or if you have a destination in mind that we haven't listed, reply to this email — our team typically responds within minutes.
nurture_day14.quiet_close: If now isn't the right time, that's completely fine. We'll be here when you're ready.
